title: Holi: the festival of colors
hook: Prahlad walks out of the fire unharmed; the next morning everyone throws color and nobody is a stranger

segments.voice: Yesterday, jati, the question about caste, and Satyakama telling the plain truth. Today, the last day of the stories, and one more fire.
screen: `YOU DON'T HAVE TO DEFEND WHAT YOU DIDN'T CHOOSE.`

segments.voice: Shiva sits in meditation on a mountain, so deep and so still that nothing reaches him. He's been there since his first wife, Sati, died. The gods need him to wake up, to marry again, to have a son who can defeat a demon. So they send the god of love, Kama, with his bow of sugarcane and his arrows of flowers, to shoot one into Shiva's heart. You've met Prahlad walking out of the fire, and Krishna coloring Radha's face in Braj. This is Holi's third story, and in parts of south India it's the one told at Holi's full moon.
screen: `SHIVA, STILL AS A MOUNTAIN.` → `KAMA DRAWS HIS FLOWER BOW.` → `HOLI'S THIRD STORY.`

segments.voice: Kama shoots. The arrow lands. And Shiva opens his third eye. Fire pours out of it, and Kama is burned to ash where he stands. His wife, Rati, falls weeping on the ashes. Here the story turns. Shiva, moved, promises that Kama will live again, but without a body. Love, from now on, will be everywhere and visible nowhere. That's why one of Kama's names is Ananga, the bodiless one. And Shiva does wake, and does marry Parvati. In parts of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, Holi's full moon is remembered as Kama Dahanam, the burning of Kama, with fires and songs of Rati's grief. So two of Holi's three stories run through fire: a bonfire that couldn't hold a child, and a fire from a god's eye that burns love's body away and sets it loose in the world. Then Krishna and Radha's morning of colors. And today is the last day of the stories. For seventy-five days you've met these people. Ganesha and his broken tusk. Rama, Sita and Hanuman. Krishna the butter thief and Krishna the charioteer. The Goddess and her nine nights. The lamps, the colors, the thread. You know them now. Tomorrow the path changes. Camp three is the practices: less story, more doing. Breath, mantra, a home shrine, a day. The stories come with you. Everyone's the same color today.
screen: `THE THIRD EYE OPENS.` · `ANANGA, LOVE WITHOUT A BODY.` · `TWO FIRES, THEN THE COLORS.` · `SEVENTY-FIVE DAYS OF STORIES.` · then, large: `EVERYONE'S THE SAME COLOR TODAY.`

segments.voice: Bring one small grudge to mind and picture it as Kama's arrow, sharp and pointed at you, then picture it burning to ash. In its place, instead of nothing, let something bodiless come: a little goodwill toward that person, invisible, but real. Breathe it in, and let it spread.
Holi. The festival of colors, the morning after the fire, where Prahlad, Radha and Kama all have a story.
Your line: everyone's the same color today. Love got loose in the world. That's the last of the stories.

screen: `DAY 96 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE BREATH YOU ALREADY HAVE.`

what it means: three Holi stories: Prahlad in the fire, Kama burned into a love that's everywhere, and Krishna and Radha's colors the morning after.
what a scholar hears: the burning of Kama is told in Kalidasa's Kumarasambhava and in the Puranas; Kama Dahanam at Holi is a southern regional custom.
